note: Manual classification of the 33 surviving held-out mutants (E5h: operators SDL, RSW, ARG, never used while the probe was built) of the final v2 (fork 5102307, phase 6) under the frozen 57-check probe and the repository tests. Two further survivors (pep.py:106:16, pep.py:107:17) lie inside the cost-ablation switch and are excluded, as in E5v4. Mutant = file:line:id as printed by e5h_survivor_diffs.py. 'harmless' = cannot change any authorization decision, effect or record on a state the API can reach. Phase 6: same 111 points, same kill results and same 33 survivors as phase 5; the delegations.py survivors moved by 29 lines. Classification carried over with updated line numbers and re-checked against e5h_survivor_diffs.py.

cache_bypass.label: cache never read/written (falls back to DB)
cache_bypass.why: the Lua read fails (arguments swapped, caught), the observed generations are not recorded so _set_grant does not cache, the entry is written under a key that is never read, or the write is skipped or fails (caught); every decision then reads PostgreSQL; performance only

equivalent.label: equivalent
equivalent.why: pep.py:79 getattr arguments swapped: ActionType is a str enum and the query parameter always has a value, so req_val is the same member; resources.py:477 conjuncts swapped; pip.py:204 min() arguments swapped; delegations.py:632 and resources.py:500 flush removed: the session commits (and flushes, running the before_flush tracking hook) at the end of the request; main.py:198 ContextVar reset removed: every request sets the address anew before any read

masked.label: masked by redundant defence
masked.why: pip.py:204 TTL not capped at the grant end: the expiry check at read time never serves an ended grant; resources.py:501 pre-commit invalidate_subject removed: the post-commit generation bump invalidates the entry; pip_invalidation.py:40/42 one of the two generation bumps (subject or object) dropped: every grant entry is keyed by both counters, so the other bump alone makes it unreachable

error_path.label: error response only
error_path.why: a 404/400 becomes 500 (None dereferenced) or a 2xx with no change, for an unknown assignment or delegation or a non-approved delegation; pep.py:81 drops the 400 for a mismatched action parameter on /access and /preview, but the gate still decides and serves the endpoint's fixed action

metadata.label: metadata no rule reads
metadata.why: user-agent string in the decision context; revoked_at and revoke_reason of a revoked delegation (shown in the API, read by no rule; the status is still REVOKED)

notification.label: revocation notice
notification.why: the notice to the requester is not sent, or loads another relationship for it

audit_loss.label: audit row of a revocation dropped
audit_loss.why: the DELEGATION_REVOKED / assignment-revoked AuditLog row is not written; the revocation itself takes effect; the probe counts decision and audit rows for access requests, not for administrative changes

workflow_state.label: non-approved delegation can be revoked
workflow_state.why: the status check before revocation is removed, so an authorised revoker can move a pending, rejected or expired delegation to REVOKED; it removes access, never grants it; no probe check revokes a non-approved delegation
